title: Three tips
summary: A pair is not enough when the receiver has just been busy.

cards.text:
The same order can grow a link a lot, or barely,
depending on how recently the receiver tipped.

If the receiver just tipped, a new good pair grows more.
The link remembers a third tip, not only the last two.

question.prompt: An isolated pair and a pair during a busy streak are the same event.
question.why: The recent receiver tip changes the size of the change.
question.simpler: Busy means a fresh third tip is still around.

question.prompt: The extra tip the rule remembers belongs to…
question.why: It is the receiver’s own recent tip, kept as a short trace.
question.simpler: No global teacher. Just a local memory of the last receiver tip.

recall.question: Does a recent receiver tip make the next good pair stronger?

deeper.note: Pfister and Gerstner wrote the triplet so one rule could fit both timing and rate experiments.

paper.title: Triplets of spikes in a model of spike timing-dependent plasticity

terms.plain: a pair plus a recent spike
terms.definition: A plasticity rule that uses three spikes, so the size of the change depends on recent rate as well as order.
